editorial:
Facing sudden doubts about her marriage, a young New York mother teams up with her larger-than-life playboy father to tail her husband. The movie mixes warm family comedy with quiet relationship drama, giving you a breezy, stylish ride through city life, old-school charm, and late-night conversations. Bill Murray and Rashida Jones make the father-daughter bond feel easy and real, while Marlon Wayans keeps the husband side grounded and believable.

The pacing is relaxed, with funny car rides, hotel stakeouts, and gentle emotional beats rather than big twists or loud action scenes. Some viewers may want more suspense or a much bigger payoff, and the story stays light even when feelings get heavy. Still, if you enjoy character-driven comedies with real heart, this is a cozy pick.
endingExplained: Laura and Felix follow Dean to Mexico after seeing him with colleague Fiona. Laura confronts Dean in his hotel room, but he insists nothing romantic happened and says his secrecy was about work. Laura chooses to trust him, and they return home to rebuild their marriage. The final scenes show Laura and Felix sharing a warm lunch, with Felix admitting he may have pushed too hard, leaving their bond stronger.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves character-driven comedies and father-daughter stories.
